verdict.rationale: FireHydrant documents API keys and bot tokens, which let a non-human identity such as an agent use the API without being tied to a user's account. The docs say a key 'by default' gets Owner permissions, which implies permissions can be changed, but they never show how to restrict a key to a narrower role or scope. missing for 10: documented per-key role/scope selection, granular least-privilege scopes (e.g. read-only or per-resource), agent-specific credential guidance, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: An API key can perform actions like any other user, and by default, it will have Owner permissions.
FireHydrant supports bot tokens to act on behalf of a computer instead of a user's account.
FireHydrant allows you to access the API with an API key using token-based authentication.
